title: Physical Structure of Planetary Nebulae. II. NGC 7662

evidence.locator: Sect. 2: the echelle spectrograph on the 4 m telescope at Kitt Peak, 21 to 23 October 1986, the [O III] 4959 and 5007 lines. Sect. 3.1: a bright 17.9 by 12.4 arcsec inner shell inside a 30.8 by 27.2 arcsec outer shell, and a faint round halo 134 arcsec across (Chu, Jacoby & Arendt 1987). Sect. 3.2: the inner shell is "an expanding prolate ellipsoidal shell with its northeast side tilted towards us"; shells in homologous expansion, speed in proportion to radius; the inner shell's major axis "is tilted by 50° against the line of sight along PA 45°", expanding at 35 ± 3 km/s in the equatorial plane and 53 ± 6 km/s along the pole; the outer shell, with the inner shell's inclination assumed, at 50 ± 5 and 60 ± 8 km/s; axial ratios 1.5 and 1.2; kinematic ages of about 700 and 1,050 years at 800 pc (Hajian & Terzian 1996). Table 1: inner shell 13 by 19.7 arcsec, 0.050 by 0.076 pc; outer shell 28 by 33.6 arcsec, 0.109 by 0.130 pc; inclination 50°, the angle between the major axis and the line of sight. The fit uses the sectors free of the fast low-ionisation emission regions.
